title: Wockhardt Reports 24% Revenue Growth to Rs 969 Crore in Q2 FY27, PAT Rises to Rs 73 Crore

contentHtml:
Mumbai: Pharmaceutical and biotechnology company Wockhardt Limited has reported a Profit After Tax (PAT) of Rs 73 crore for the second quarter of FY 2026-27, registering a 24% year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 969 crore, compared to Rs 782 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.

The company’s EBITDA for Q2 FY27 stood at Rs 165 crore, compared to Rs 160 crore in Q2 FY26. Excluding pre-launch expenses associated with Zaynich, EBITDA stood at Rs 201 crore. For the first half of FY27, the company recorded revenue of Rs 1,898 crore, registering a 25% growth over Rs 1,520 crore in the corresponding period last year. EBITDA increased by 35% to Rs 353 crore, while PAT stood at Rs 180 crore.

Wockhardt’s biotechnology operations recorded revenue of Rs 252 crore during Q2 FY27, registering 68% growth compared to the corresponding quarter of the previous year. For the first half of FY27, biotechnology revenue reached Rs 487 crore, reflecting 87% growth. The Emerging Markets biotechnology segment recorded approximately 110% growth, supported by business partnerships and expansion in Brazil, Thailand, Egypt, Algeria and Latin American markets.

In its domestic and international operations, the India Branded Business generated revenue of Rs 146 crore during Q2 FY27, registering 8% growth, while the Emerging Markets business recorded revenue of Rs 310 crore, reflecting 52% growth. The UK business reported revenue of GBP 28 million, while the Irish business recorded half-yearly revenue of EUR 11 million, registering 13% growth.

The company also highlighted developments in its novel antibiotic discovery programme. Five novel antibiotics, namely Emrok, Emrok O, Miqnaf, Zaynich and Foviscu, have successfully completed Phase III clinical trials, according to the company.

Zaynich received US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval on May 29, 2026, for the treatment of complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI), including pyelonephritis. The company described it as the first India-discovered and developed drug to receive US FDA approval. It also received approval from the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) for manufacturing and marketing in India on August 25, 2026. Its European Medicines Agency (EMA) review process is currently progressing.

Miqnaf (nafithromycin) has been approved and launched in India. The removal of its supply condition by the Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI) is expected to facilitate wider patient access. Meanwhile, Foviscu (WCK 4282) has successfully completed Phase II and Phase III clinical trials in India, and its New Drug Application (NDA) has been filed.

During the quarter, Wockhardt reported 24 international product filings, 18 approvals and 11 launches. The company also received approval for Emrok O and Emrok injection in Uganda. Its biosimilar programme recorded two filings and four approvals, while its New Chemical Entity (NCE) programme recorded one filing and two approvals.

According to the company, Wockhardt filed seven patents and received six patent grants during Q2 FY27, taking its cumulative patent filings to 3,298 and its total granted patent portfolio to 865.
